data.title: U.S. Dept. of Justice says states should post $1.9B bond in Paramount suit
data.description:
The U.S. Dept. of Justice wants state attorneys general and a trade union suing to block Paramount Skydance's $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) to post a $1.9 billion bond to cover late fees that result from their litigation.

"None of these cases provides a legitimate basis to disregard Section 16’s plain text requiring private persons to post a 'proper bond' before a preliminary injunction may issue," attorneys for the DOJ  wrote in a filing on Monday.

Last Wednesday Paramount (PSKY) continued its campaign to have plaintiffs in a lawsuit seeking to block its merger with Warner Bros. (WBD) post a $1.9 billion surety bond to cover the company’s losses, including ticking fees, if it ultimately prevails.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount (PSKY) must pay Warner Bros. (WBD) shareholders $650M per quarter beginning October 1. Because the trial is set for March 2027, Paramount would be required to pay $1.3B in ticking fees plus another $190M in incremental financing costs and legal fees.

The plaintiffs, which include twelve state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, argue that Paramount (PSKY) is ineligible for a bond since it was Paramount that agreed to halt the merger.

The judge overseeing the case, Araceli Martínez-Olguín, previously declined to order a bond in July. The federal judge has scheduled a trial start date for  March 2027.

News of the DOJ's push for the states to post a bond was earlier reported by Bloomberg.

data.title: Stocks to watch on Tuesday after hours: MU, IVR, FTAI
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages concluded lower on Tuesday as investors prepared for the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) lost -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished -0.7%.

Now, here are a few stocks to watch in after-hours trading:

  • Micron Technology (MU) appointed tech sector veteran Deirdre Hanford to serve as president of Micron Research Labs, the memory maker's long-horizon research institution, which was announced last month and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.
  • Invesco Mortgage Capital (IVR) posted a slight decline in its estimated book value per common share to $7.74 as of August 31 from $7.75 as of July 31. Shares edged up 0.3% at press time.
  • FTAI Aviation (FTAI) authorized a new $500M share repurchase program to buy back its outstanding ordinary shares. The stock drove up 4%.

data.title: Invesco Mortgage Capital sees decline in August-end estimated book value per share
data.description:
Invesco Mortgage Capital (IVR) on Tuesday reported a decline in its estimated book value per common share to $7.74 as of August 31 from $7.75 as of July 31.

Unrestricted cash and unencumbered investments reduced to $534.7M from $549.3M.

Investment portfolio as of August end reached $8.3B from $8.1B at the end of the prior month. The portfolio consisted of 30-year fixed-rate pass-through comprising 80.3% of agency RMBS, agency CMO 0.7%, and agency CMBS 10.8%. Total agency to-be-announced comprised 8.2%.

Repurchase agreement borrowings increased to $6.9B from $6.5B. 

Debt-to-equity ratio stood at 6.8x on August 31, while the economic debt-to-equity ratio was 7.5x.

The mortgage REIT maintained its monthly cash dividend at $0.12 per share, payable on October 15 to stockholders of record at the close of business on September 28.

data.title: Baosheng Media receives Nasdaq bid-price deficiency notice; shares down
data.description:
• Baosheng Media Group (BAOS) received a Nasdaq deficiency notice after its shares traded below the $1 minimum bid-price requirement for 30 consecutive business days.
  • Baosheng has until March 9, 2027 to regain compliance under the 180-day compliance period.
  • The company may also use a reverse stock split, which must be completed no later than 10 business days before March 9, 2027, to regain compliance.
  • BAOS shares down 8.8% post-market.

data.title: Micron appoints industry veteran Hanford to lead its research institution
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) appointed tech sector veteran Deirdre Hanford to serve as president of Micron Research Labs, the memory maker's long-horizon research institution, which was announced last month and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho. 

The global research institution is backed by a $10B investment from Micron over the next 10 years. Its research will include critical memory process technologies, future memory and compute architectures, advanced packaging and next-generation semiconductor manufacturing.

"Micron Research Labs was created to pursue the breakthroughs that will define the future of memory, compute and AI, and Deirdre is uniquely qualified to lead that mission," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer of Micron Technology. "She combines deep semiconductor industry expertise with a proven ability to build partnerships, inspire collaboration and turn ambitious ideas into lasting impact."

Hanford spent nearly 40 years at Synopsys (SNPS). Her roles included chief security officer, co-general manager of the Design Group and executive vice president of customer engagement. She currently serves on the UC Berkeley College of Engineering Advisory Board, the MIT School of Engineering Dean's Advisory Council and the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders.

data.title: FTAI Aviation announces $500M buyback plan; shares in focus
data.description:
• FTAI Aviation (FTAI) authorized a new $500M share repurchase program to buy back its outstanding ordinary shares.
  • The company plans to use cash on its balance sheet to fund the buybacks.
  • The program will run through September 30, 2029, unless completed earlier.
  • The shares may be repurchased through the open market or private transactions, depending on market conditions.
  • The program does not require the company to repurchase any specific amount, and the timing and size of purchases will depend on its share price and market conditions.
  • On the market side, the FTAI stock traded nearly 4% higher at ~$182.99 in the after-hours trading session.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Beta Bionics plans $125M public offering; shares down
data.description:
• Beta Bionics (BBNX) announced plans for an underwritten public offering of $125M of common stock.
  • The company also intends to grant underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $18.75M of common stock.
  • Beta Bionics expects to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes, including commercialization of Mint, manufacturing expansion, R&D, clinical development and working capital.
  • Funds may also support product enhancements and potential strategic opportunities, alongside operating expenses.
  • BBNX shares down 8% post-market.
